title: Distortions
objective: Recognise at knowledge level why distortion can occur during fabrication and welding, how it can affect a component, and why prevention or correction decisions must follow approved technical requirements.

verified_internal_assessment_criteria: IAC0301 — List and describe causes of distortions — 50%
IAC0302 — List and describe methods of correcting distortions — 50%
curriculum_traceability.primary_source: QCTO occupational curriculum hosted by CHIETA — Curriculum-6.pdf

safety_boundary: Knowledge and safety-awareness only. This lesson explains distortion conceptually. It does not provide welding parameters, heating instructions, mechanical straightening procedures, equipment setup, or step-by-step methods for correcting distortion. Practical correction belongs in authorised occupational training under competent supervision.

sections.heading: 1. What is distortion?
sections.body: Distortion is an unwanted change in the shape or dimensions of a component. In fabrication work it can occur when material is affected unevenly during joining or other thermal processes.

sections.heading: 2. Why distortion matters
sections.body: A distorted component may no longer match its drawing, dimensions, alignment or assembly requirements. Recognising distortion is therefore part of understanding fabrication quality.

sections.heading: 3. Causes of distortion
sections.body: Distortion can be associated with uneven thermal expansion and contraction, the shape and thickness of material, joint arrangement, restraint and the sequence of fabrication work. The exact cause must be assessed against the job requirements rather than guessed.

sections.heading: 4. Recognising the effect
sections.body: Distortion may show as changes in alignment, angle, flatness or overall dimensions. The important learning principle is to compare the component with its approved drawing, specification or workplace requirement.

sections.heading: 5. Prevention and correction concepts
sections.body: Fabrication planning can include controls intended to limit distortion, and workplaces may use approved methods to deal with distortion that has occurred. The suitable response depends on the material, component and authorised procedure.

sections.heading: 6. Do not improvise
sections.body: Trying to correct distortion without knowing the material, specification or approved method can create additional defects or hazards. Correction decisions belong within authorised workplace procedures.

sections.heading: 7. Stop and refer
sections.body: If the cause, acceptable tolerance or approved response is uncertain, stop and refer the component to a competent trainer or supervisor before practical action is taken.
